Alright, let me think this through. I've been working this land for 50 years, so most of what I do comes from what I've seen work on my own fields, plus what my neighbors do. I'll talk through each crop.

---

**My land and how I split it**

I have 10.1 mu total. Like most folks around here, I do wheat-maize double crop on the good flat ground — that's 7 mu. The other 3.1 mu I put to chili because the price has been decent and one of my daughters-in-law helps with picking. Chili brings in cash, but wheat and maize keep the family fed and the grain bin full. I don't want to put everything on chili because if the price crashes one year, we'd be in trouble.

---

**Winter wheat (7 mu)**

I plant around October 8-12, right after the maize comes off. I use Jimai 22 seed — my neighbor Old Wang has been growing it for years and it stands up well to the dry spring wind. About 12-13 kg seed per mu, a bit heavy because at my age I'd rather have a thick stand than worry about tillering later. Costs me around 55 yuan/mu for seed.

For fertilizer, I put down a bag of compound (15-15-15) before planting, that's about 40 kg/mu — gives me about 6 kg N as base. Then at returning-green/jointing in late March I topdress urea, about 25 kg/mu (that's another 11-12 kg N). So roughly 17-18 kg N/mu total. The extension fellow last year said I could do less, maybe 15, but I've always done it this way and I'm not changing at 67. If the wheat looks pale at jointing I'll add a bit more. Some P and K comes from the compound — I don't buy extra.

Irrigation: winter water in late November if the soil is dry, then jointing water, heading water, and grain-fill water. Usually 3-4 times. Well water is metered, costs me maybe 25-30 yuan/mu each round. If it rains well in spring I can skip one.

Herbicide once in early spring for the winter weeds (about 15 yuan/mu). If aphids show up at heading I'll spray once.

Tillage: I hire the rotary tiller man from the village, he charges 40 yuan/mu. Can't do it by hand anymore.

I expect about 450 kg/mu. Last year I got 460, year before 420. Depends on the spring weather.

---

**Summer maize (7 mu)**

Right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The turnaround is tight — maybe 3-5 days. I use Zhengdan 958 seed, hybrid, about 2 kg/mu, direct-seeded with the hired planter. Seed cost around 35 yuan/mu.

Fertilizer: I do one base shot of compound at planting with the seeder, maybe 30 kg/mu. Then topdress urea at big flare stage (大喇叭口), around 20 kg/mu. Comes to about 14-15 kg N/mu total. Maize doesn't need as much as wheat in my experience, plus if you put too much on it falls over before harvest.

Irrigation: usually once at big flare if July is dry. Some years the rain is enough and I skip. 0-2 times.

One herbicide spray after planting for grass weeds. Rarely spray for pests unless I see corn borer holes.

No tillage — direct seed into wheat stubble. That's how everyone does it now.

Yield: around 500 kg/mu. Good year 550, bad year 400.

---

**Chili (3.1 mu)**

This is the money crop but also the hardest work. I transplant seedlings around late April when the soil warms up — I buy seedlings from the cooperative at about 180 yuan/mu worth. Variety is a dried-chili type, Sanying or similar, whatever the cooperative has.

Before transplanting I put down farmyard manure if I have any (from my two pigs), plus about 50 kg/mu of compound fertilizer. Through the season I topdress urea twice — once after the plants establish, once at flowering/fruit set. Total N maybe 22-25 kg/mu. Chili is hungry, you can't skimp.

Irrigation: 4-5 times, chili can't handle drought. Furrow irrigation from the well.

Pesticide: this is where it gets expensive. Spray for thrips and aphids 3-4 times, and I have to spray fungicide for anthracnose — if that hits you lose half the crop. Maybe 200-250 yuan/mu total in sprays.

Labor is the killer. Transplanting takes my wife, me, and our daughter-in-law about a week. Then picking starts late July and goes through October, 4-5 rounds. My son sometimes comes back from the city on weekends. If we can't manage I hire two village women at 120 yuan/day for the picking peaks.

Yield: I aim for about 250 kg/mu of dried chili. Price last year was around 18 yuan/kg so that's 4500/mu gross if it works out. But anthracnose can cut it in half.

---

**Money situation**

Total cash out for inputs I figure around 9,000-10,000 yuan for the year. Most of that is the chili. The wheat and maize pay for themselves and feed us. Chili is where the real money is, but also where the risk is. I keep some cash back — at my age I don't want to be caught short if the well motor breaks.
